answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation tied to verifiable work history. A new agent starts at its nadir: no stake, no history, no trust. To earn influence it must post a small bond and complete attested tasks, so a hundred fake identities cost a hundred bonds and a hundred real work records. An onyx ledger records each agent's history immutably, so a bad actor cannot erase a bad reputation by re-registering. Sybils still appear, but each carries the same cost as a real participant, and the plume of cheap fakes collapses because none can afford the stake and history needed to matter.
